compliance.nebs: the Regulatory Compliance table lists NEBS GR-1089 under EMC and NEBS GR-63 under Environment; separately the datasheet's Key Benefits line reads 'Ideal for Core, Edge, and Central Office deployments (NEBS Level 3)'. Both wordings are carried because they are different claims and neither document reconciles them

features.breakout: service ports 0-19 can individually break out into 4x25GE or 4x10GE; if any of ports 0-19 is in breakout mode the corresponding lower-column port is disabled (HIG Port Overview). Ports 20-39 are 40GE/100GE only
features.deployment: functions standalone or as a node in a cluster from 4 Tbps up to 192 Tbps; interoperable with the rest of the S9700 series using an S9705-48D or S9725-64E as the fabric (datasheet Key Features). Keyed `deployment` rather than `role`, which is reserved for the structural role each GROUP carries
features.fabric-ports: the thirteen 400G QSFP-DD ports are FABRIC ports and are for connecting to the fabric ports of an S9705-48D fabric switch only, not for service traffic (HIG Port Overview)
features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD DAC, AEC and AOC up to 100 m - the fabric ports take cables, and the datasheet's Compatible Fabric Cable Types list carries no optical transceiver
features.optics-qsfp28: 100GE QSFP28 SR4, LR4, ER4 and ZR4, up to 80 km (datasheet Compatible Transceiver Types)
features.optics-sfp-plus: NOT STATED. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types block lists 100GE QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4 only and its Compatible Fabric Cable Types block lists 400GE QSFP-DD DAC/AEC/AOC; neither names anything for the two 10G SFP+ management ports, and the HIG's Connecting the Transceiver section names no part either. The cage takes what an SFP+ cage takes; which optics UfiSpace qualifies in it is unrecorded here rather than inferred - see the sfp-plus-optics gap
features.routing: full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) support (datasheet Key Features)

management.console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console, both lettered IOIOI

platform.tcam: Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM for additional table sizes

configs.description: The chassis as HIG Figure 7's rear elevation and the vendor's own rear product render both draw it - four FAN-803816-HC exhaust fans and two PSU-202-AESR 2000 W AC supplies with C20 appliance inlets and red latches, front-to-back airflow, and the fifty-five traffic, fabric and management ports empty. The HIG rates the feed at 200-240 V and notes that on a single 110 VAC source each supply delivers only 1000 W, at which point hot-swapping a supply is no longer supported. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document; see the chassis-sku gap.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: Dual 2000 W DC supplies (PSU-202-DESR, two-post screw terminal under a hinged plastic cover) with the same FAN-803816-HC exhaust fans. Datasheet input -40 to -72 V at 60 A; the HIG's DC section gives the maximum system consumption as 1434 W against the AC build's 1422 W. No held image of THIS device shows a DC supply - see the dc-build-unphotographed gap.
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the four front-panel lamps (SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1), the PSU FRU lamp, the Fan FRU lamp and the management-port lamps, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Every QSFP28 and QSFP-DD column prints two round lamps between its two port numerals and nothing states what they mean, nor which lamp of a pair serves which of the two ports. The pairing written here is derived from the printed order alone - the legend reads '▲n lamp lamp m▼', so the left lamp is taken to serve the upper port n - and port 12's single lamp is placed where a pair's left lamp sits for the same reason. That is the one thing in this device's LED model that is not read off a source. Every port lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic

gaps.note: HIG Figure 4 names the two-digit seven-segment display 'Beacon LED' and the datasheet's LED list carries a 'Beacon' row, so unlike the S9600-72XC's identical-looking display this one at least has a name. What it DISPLAYS is still unstated: section 10's Verifying System Operation covers the four panel lamps and the two FRU lamps and never mentions it, so whether the digits show a chassis or cluster ID, a POST code or a fault code is not established. The component therefore carries no state vocabulary and its skin draws the all-segments '88' the vendor's own artwork draws.
gaps.wanted: a NOS or BMC reference that documents the front-panel beacon display

gaps.note: The bezel measured on this faceplate is 15.6 x 8.9 mm; ufispace/seg7-status-2@1 is 17.2 x 9.5, measured on the S9600-72XC, and is the closest of the three UfiSpace seven-segment contracts (the other two are 12.8 wide, a fifth too small). The part is used as it stands rather than forking a fourth contract off a 1.6 mm difference read from a 3.13 px/mm figure, but the placed display is about a millimetre larger than the metal.
gaps.wanted: an orthographic vendor front elevation of the S9700-53DX, or a square-on photograph

gaps.note: The reset feature on the panel is a white printed ring about 2.4 mm across around a dark pinhole about 1 mm across, measured at 20x on HIG Figure 8. common/reset-button@1 is 4.0 x 4.0 with `size: estimated` in its own provenance, so the library part is the softer number - but it is the part a person can name and it is used. The consequence is visible: the placed button laps roughly 0.9 mm onto the left edge of the printed system-lamp label block. Fixing it by moving the label block would move a measured number to suit an estimated one, so it is filed instead.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace mechanical drawing of the front panel, or a resized reset component

gaps.note: The datasheet orders PSU-202-DESR and the HIG has a full DC power section with its own maximum (1434 W), so the DC build certainly exists - but every image held for THIS device shows the AC supply: HIG Figure 7's rear elevation, HIG Figures 5 and 6 (which are the AC unit's own drawings), and the vendor's rear product render. The DC configuration here seats ufispace/psu-202-dc@1, whose face was measured on the S9600-56DX's rear photograph, and that is an inference from a sibling chassis rather than a reading of this one. The two routers order the same PSU part numbers, which is why it is reasonable; it is recorded because it is still not sourced here.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of an S9700-53DX with DC supplies fitted

gaps.note: HIG Figure 7 carries no model name anywhere in it, and the S9700-23D's guide is illustrated with a rear elevation of the same fan and PSU arrangement. This family is exactly where a vendor reuses artwork, so the rear here cannot be certified as a picture of THIS model the way the front can - the front figures letter 'S9700-53DX' and draw this model's own port inventory. What supports the rear is not the figure: the FRU part numbers (FAN-803816-HC, PSU-202-AESR/DESR) and their dimensions come from this device's own datasheet and its own Component Physical Information table, the 4-fan and 2-PSU counts from Figure 4's callouts, and the vendor's rear product render of this SKU shows the same face. The geometry is the figure's; the inventory is this document's.
gaps.wanted: a rear elevation that letters the model, or a dimensioned rear mechanical drawing

gaps.note: The HIG counts the rail hardware exactly - five attachment pins per side, ten in total, plus one M4 inner-rail screw per side - and the vendor's angle render shows those pins as silver studs, so the COUNT and the KIND are sourced. No held figure dimensions them along the depth, and no held figure shows the underside at all, so every position on the two side faces and the compliance sticker on the bottom is ESTIMATED. They are drawn rather than left blank so the faces carry honest content, and this entry is what says which part of that content is a measurement.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace mechanical drawing of the chassis sides and underside

gaps.note: Neither held document names an optic for the two 10G SFP+ management ports. Searched the datasheet for 'SFP+' - three hits, all of them the port count in the physical list, the LED list and the Key Features - and its Compatible Transceiver Types and Compatible Fabric Cable Types blocks cover QSFP28 and QSFP-DD and stop; searched the HIG for 'transceiver' - its Connecting the Transceiver section is a procedure with no part numbers. So the group carries a sentence recording the silence rather than a list borrowed from a sibling datasheet.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace qualified-optics list for the S9700 series

gaps.note: No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document. The datasheet's Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only, and the HIG names the product S9700-53DX in its title, its overview and its dimensions table without printing a number. The configurations here therefore carry no `part-numbers`. The S9510-28DC's history is the warning: 'no SKU exists' was written there on exactly this evidence and was false, so this says only that we hold no document naming one.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9700 core-edge line

gaps.note: Neither this datasheet nor this HIG publishes a per-FRU wattage for FAN-803816-HC. The datasheet names it only as an ordering line and the HIG's power sections give the SYSTEM maxima (1434 W DC, 1422 W AC, both at 45 C with optics fully populated and 100% traffic) and the 2000 W per-circuit provisioning reserve - all three are the box, not the module. Searched this HIG for 'watt', 'Power' and 'consumption': every hit belongs to the system figures or to the PSU-202 ordering lines. So the module total for this chassis is a floor, and L27/L29 standing on the fan is the record of that.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-803816-HC

attrs.note: datasheet - Specifications, Environmental, Performance, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied; note that the NEBS claim is split across two places in the datasheet and both wordings are carried.

band-legends.note: A RULE THAT STOPS PARTWAY WAS SPECIFICALLY LOOKED FOR HERE, AND IT DOES STOP - twice, and both times the metal really stops it. (1) The green band covers the UPPER QSFP28 block and there is no band under the lower block: ports 20-39 carry the same ▲ numeral lamp lamp numeral ▼ legend, printed white directly on the black metal at y 73.6. The legend rule is carried to the end; the PAINT is not, and that is the vendor's doing. (2) The pink band's per-column legend ends after port 12 with an up-arrow, a numeral and one lamp, because there is no thirteenth partner port. Both readings were taken against a control in the same image: the '20', '21' ... '39' numerals under the lower block are the same white ink at the same size and the same distance from the lens as the area under it that carries nothing, and they resolve cleanly at 7x, so the blank metal below them is a reading and not a resolution limit. Within a column the offsets from the column centre are ▲ -7.8, upper numeral -5.2, lamp -1.93, lamp +1.93, lower numeral +5.2, ▼ +8.0 mm, measured once on columns 1 and 2 of the green band and reused; the QSFP-DD band reads -7.7 / -5.0 / ±1.88 / +5.0 / +8.4 on its tighter 19 mm pitch. The arrows are drawn as `path:` marks because U+25B2 and U+25BC rasterise as empty boxes.

bands.note: drawing - the two coloured bands are real paint and both were sampled: the QSFP28 band is #4a692e green and runs x 44.7-274.0, y 8.2-12.8, ABOVE the upper block only; the QSFP-DD band is #d68998 pink and runs x 282.4-429.7, y 23.6-29.6, above the upper fabric row. The HIG says what they mean in as many words - the service ports (green in its figure) are packet-based Ethernet ports, and the fabric ports (red) connect only to the fabric ports of the S9705-48D fabric switch - so the colour is a legend and is drawn as one.

beacon.note: drawing plus a named callout, which is the part the S9600-72XC could not get. A two-digit seven-segment display sits at the top right, bezel x 412.3-427.9 and y 5.6-14.5 measured off fig-0016, and HIG Figure 4's callout list names it in as many words: 'Beacon LED'. The datasheet's LED list also carries a 'Beacon' row. So it is modelled as ufispace/seg7-status-2@1, the 17.2 x 9.5 contract measured on the S9600-72XC - 1.6 mm wider and 0.6 mm taller than the bezel measured here, which is the closest of the three UfiSpace seven-segment parts (seg7-beacon-s9611 and seg7-status-2-sm are both 12.8 wide, a fifth too small). What the digits actually SHOW is still unstated and is recorded in the beacon-semantics gap.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm or 17.17" x 30" x 3.45"', 'Weight: 21.14 kg or 46.61 lb (Without FRU)'; the HIG's Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple and the same weight. 436 is the BODY and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance paragraph states both numbers in one sentence - 'The S9700-53DX chassis width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and is shipped with an adjustable mounting rail kit suited for standard 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks' - so the ears are the 46.7 mm difference and are not drawn. 87.7 mm is 1.98 rack units, which is why the datasheet calls it 2RU. The 762 mm depth is the chassis without FRUs; the HIG adds that the fan handle projects 1 inch (25 mm) and the PSU handle 1.5 inches (38 mm), which is clearance rather than body and is carried on those components' relief.

colour.note: photo/drawing - the chassis is a very dark neutral grey. Sampled from fig-0016 the bare metal between the port blocks is #2b2b28 and the left field #2a2a2a; #33332e is carried, a touch lighter than the sample so the black cage apertures still read against it, and the vendor's angle render agrees it is grey rather than true black. THE GANGED-CAGE SHELLS WERE SAMPLED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN ASSUMED SILVER: the median of the shell pixels is #cecece, a neutral light grey with no blue in it, and #c8cacc is used. The bright shell behind the portrait USB socket is drawn as its own decor pill, because std/usb-a draws the opening and its blue tongue and nothing around it, and a dark connector on a dark faceplate is invisible.

connector-orientation.note: measured, not assumed, and it differs between the two cage families on this one panel. QSFP28: each column is a 1x2 belly-to-belly ganged cage and the two rows MIRROR - a column profile through fig-0016 shows the upper port's graded bezel band BELOW its black face (y 102-107) and the lower port's ABOVE its face (y 122-123), with the perforated EMI strip between them at y 108-121. std/qsfp-ganged draws its cage lip at the BOTTOM of an upright opening, so the LOWER port of every pair is rotate: 180 and the upper is unrotated - grid rows 2 and 4 rotated, rows 1 and 3 not. The stacked SFP+ pair and the stacked RJ45 pair mirror the same way. QSFP-DD: the two rows are SEPARATE single-height ganged shells and, at 7x, they are drawn IDENTICALLY rather than mirrored - both show the same bright lip inside the same edge - so both rows are placed unrotated. That difference between the two families on one faceplate is the reason it is written down. The RJ45 pair was read in a zoomed crop before being trusted: the upper jack's latch notch is at the TOP of its opening and the lower jack's at the BOTTOM, and the lower jack is the one carrying two green lamps in its bottom corners, which is what makes it the out-of-band port rather than the console. The USB 2.0 Type-A socket is PORTRAIT (5.2 wide by 11.9 tall) so std/usb-a is rotated 90.

front-grid.note: drawing - the QSFP28 field sits on ONE four-row grid and the pitch was taken from a feature that repeats once per PORT, never from the drawn cage shells. Row centres are the black cage openings measured down a single column of fig-0016 (x 368-412): 77-99, 126-147, 172-194 and 220-241 px, centres 88, 136.5, 183 and 230.5, which least-squares to 18.20 + 15.57k mm with no residual over 0.35 mm. The four rows read as two visual bands only because the two upper rows share one cage shell and the two lower rows share another; the pitch does not change across the gap between them. THE QSFP-DD PORTS SHARE THE SAME GRID: their own openings read 34.32 and 48.78 mm against the grid's 33.77 and 49.34, half a millimetre, so they are carried on rows 2 and 3 rather than given a second set of numbers. Note that the row centres here are the BLACK OPENING centres; including each cage's graded bezel band moves an aperture centre by about a millimetre, which is three pixels at 3.04 px/mm and is inside what this figure resolves.

fru-reuse.note: The fan is FAN-803816-HC, named in this datasheet's Available to Order block, and ufispace/fan-803816-hc@1 already carries exactly the dimensions this HIG's Component Physical Information table gives - 'Fan (W x D x H) 3.19" x 4.45" x 3.21" (81 x 113 x 81.5 mm)', so an 81 x 81.5 face - and the same 25 mm handle projection this guide publishes. It is used unchanged. That component was built from the S9700-23D's guide by another author; this device corroborates its size table and its ordering line independently rather than restating them from it. The PSUs are PSU-202-AESR/DESR and ufispace/psu-202-ac@1 / -dc@1 are 50.5 x 40.2 against this HIG's 'PSU (W x D x H) 1.99 x 14.17" x 1.58" (50.5 x 360 x 40 mm)' - the 0.2 mm on the face height is the 56DX's own measurement against this table's rounded 40, and is not worth a second contract.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9700-53DX end of life end of sale announcement' - no announcement found; the vendor's telco core-edge product page, the Open Compute Project's S9700-53DX specification listing and the hardware installation guide are all live. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.

mgmt-block.note: drawing - the left column of the faceplate, top to bottom: the '0 ▲ ▼ 1' legend at y 10.2, the stacked 10G SFP+ management pair (shell x 22.4-38.3, ports at y 19.42 and 32.56), the white four-legend lamp block with its lamps in a column at x 15.88, the reset pinhole, the 'IOIOI' legend over the micro-USB console socket, the portrait USB 2.0 Type-A socket with its trident symbol under it, and the stacked RJ45 pair (console above, out-of-band below) with the 'IOIOI ▲ ▼ network' legend under it at y 75.4. Every one of those is a Figure 4 callout by name. The RJ45 pair's row pitch is 12.46 mm, which is BELOW std/rj45's 14 mm bezel, so std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) is the part - the same finding this library has made on every other stacked UfiSpace jack. RESET IS NOT LETTERED ON THE METAL: at 20x the panel carries a white ring around a dark pinhole and no word, so none is printed here; 'Reset' is Figure 4's callout, not silkscreen. common/reset-button@1 is 4.0 mm against that measured 2.4 mm ring - the component's own size is `estimated` and this figure is the better measurement - so the placed part laps about 0.9 mm onto the left edge of the printed lamp-label block. That is a known cosmetic compromise, recorded rather than fixed by moving a measured number.

panel-metal.note: THE BRIGHT SHELL AROUND EACH GANGED BLOCK IS PANEL, NOT PART, AND ITS COLOUR WAS SAMPLED RATHER THAN ASSUMED - the median of the shell pixels in fig-0016 is #cecece, a neutral light grey, and #c8cacc is carried here. std/ parts draw the opening and stop, so every ganged block is drawn as a light decor rectangle with the apertures placed on it: twenty QSFP28 column shells 19.8 x 26.6 (ten in the upper band at y 12.68, ten in the lower at y 43.82), three QSFP-DD pair shells 41.5 x 10.9 per row plus one 19.8 wide single for port 12, a 15.9 x 26.6 shell behind the stacked SFP+ pair and a 16.3 x 25.0 shell behind the stacked RJ45 pair. Without them a dark cage on a dark faceplate is simply invisible. The same reasoning puts a white printed block under the four system lamp legends, which fig-0015 prints dark-on-white at x 10.54-14.37, y 27.92-39.09.

port-leds.note: drawing - the arrangement is ONE lamp per port, in the band that labels its block, and it was counted rather than assumed. Every column of every block prints two round lamps between its two numerals, so ten columns x two lamps x two QSFP28 blocks is forty lamps for forty ports, and six columns x two plus port 12's single lamp is thirteen for thirteen. Lamp diameter reads about 1.7 mm and common/led-dot@1 at 2.0 is the closest part that fits the 3.86 mm lamp pitch. WHICH lamp of a pair serves which port is NOT stated anywhere and is recorded in the port-led-semantics gap; the left-lamp-is-the- upper-port reading used here is taken from the printed order '▲n lamp lamp m▼' alone.

power.note: datasheet 'Typical power: 563 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG states the maximum twice, once per build: 'The maximum system power consumption is 1434 watts' in the DC section and 1422 in the AC section, and unlike the typical figure these ARE qualified, in a note printed beside each - 'Temperature: 45C, Optics: full populated, Traffic: 100% load'. 1434 is carried as power-max-w because max means the highest of the two builds, and the 12 W difference is recorded here rather than as a conflict: they are two builds, not two readings. Note that power-envelope therefore describes the TYPICAL figure's scope and not the maximum's, which is fully-configured and says so in this sentence. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set: the fans publish no draw at all, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor. Provisioning reserve 2000 W per circuit (HIG). PSU rating 2000 W per supply from the ordering lines; on a single 110 VAC feed the HIG derates each supply to 1000 W and warns that hot-swap is then no longer supported.

psu-build.note: BOTH THE GUIDE AND THE PHOTOGRAPH SHOW THE AC BUILD HERE, which is the opposite of the S9600-56DX's situation and is stated so nobody reads the two devices as contradicting each other. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation and the vendor's own rear product render (photos/s9700-53dx-3-view) both draw the same face: a square-grid intake vent on the left under the status lamp, the C20 appliance inlet with its cord clip to its right and a red latch at the top right. The HIG's AC section names the cable as 'IEC60320 C19', which is the plug a C20 inlet takes. The datasheet orders both builds - PSU-202-AESR and PSU-202-DESR, 2000 W each, exhaust airflow - so the DC build is modelled as a configuration using ufispace/psu-202-dc@1, whose artwork was measured on the S9600-56DX's DC photograph and NOT on any image of this device; no held image of this device shows a DC supply, and that is recorded in the dc-build-unphotographed gap rather than left to look sourced.

qsfp28-layout.note: drawing, measured twice in two different images and agreeing to one pixel. In fig-0016 the black cage openings of columns 4-10 sit at 391.0, 465.5, 539.0, 612.0, 685.5, 758.5 and 832.0 px (columns 1-3 are under the yellow breakout highlight and were not used); in fig-0015 the white ▲/▼ pairs printed in the green band give column centres of 170.0, 243.0, 316.75, 390.0, 463.0, 536.75, 610.0, 683.25, 757.0 and 830.0 px, which after the one-pixel origin difference between the two figures land within 1 px of the openings everywhere they overlap. Least squares over the openings gives a uniform 73.5 px = 23.478 mm pitch and a first column at 52.54 mm. The drawn opening is 17.6 mm wide against the registry's 18.5 mm std/qsfp-ganged aperture, and the registry wins for an opening size; the bright shell around each column measures 19.8 mm and is drawn as panel decor - see panel-metal. Numbering is Figure 8's own and is COLUMN-MAJOR within each band: the upper band carries 0/1 in column 1 through 18/19 in column 10, the lower band 20/21 through 38/39. The HIG's port table confirms it - 'Port ID 0 ~ 19 ... 40GE/100GE (10GE/25GE in breakout)' and '20 ~ 39 ... 40GE/100GE'.

qsfpdd-layout.note: drawing - thirteen 400G fabric ports at the right of the panel, in three 2x2 groups plus one odd port, which is the shape the count forces and is drawn exactly so. Black opening centres in fig-0016 are 921.5, 981.0, 1055.0, 1114.5, 1188.0, 1246.5 and 1322.0 px = 292.43, 311.43, 335.06, 354.07, 377.55, 396.24 and 420.35 mm. The pitch INSIDE a pair is 19.00, 19.01 and 18.69 mm and BETWEEN pairs 23.64 and 23.48; the 19.0 is carried uniformly - the third pair's second column is written 396.55 rather than the measured 396.24, one pixel over, because 19.0 is the registry's own std/qsfp-dd width and three readings of one pitch that come out 19.00, 19.01 and 18.69 are one pitch measured three times, not three pitches. Ports 0-11 are the three pairs, upper row even and lower row odd, and port 12 sits alone in the UPPER row at the right with no partner below it - the pink band prints '▲12' and a single lamp there and stops, which is a rule ending where the hardware ends rather than a rule left unfinished.

rear-layout.note: drawing - HIG Figure 7's rear elevation at 3.0550 px/mm across and 3.0445 down, which is the most nearly orthographic figure in this intake. Four fan faces on an 84.44 mm pitch, read off the four green status lamps (figure x 73.6, 331.5, 589.5 and 847.6 px - three intervals of 258.0, 258.0 and 258.1 px, a flat feature painted on the face rather than the red release tabs, which project and shrink across the frame) and anchored through ufispace/fan-803816-hc@1's own lamp position (18.5, 21.0 within its 81 x 81.5 face) to put the first bay at x 0.20, y 2.75. Fan 0 is flush with the chassis's left edge - the leftmost red release tab starts at the body edge itself - and the 3.44 mm between an 81 mm module and the next bay is the chassis web. Then the grounding column (a silver two-hole plate at x 348.1-359.7, y 6.4-39.3, an earth symbol at 362.5-368.7, a captive screw knob 7.5 mm across centred at 358.8, 45.4, and the FAN 0|1|2|3 position key at y 56.7 and 62.6) and the two PSU bays at x 372.7, 50.5 wide and 40.2 tall, PSU0 over PSU1 with their tops at y 4.4 and 46.5. The bay legends PSU0 and PSU1 are chassis silkscreen at x 430: which bay is 0 is a position fact and cannot live on an interchangeable FRU.

sources.note: UfiSpace S9700-53DX datasheet for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, power, environment and compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9700-53DX Hardware Installation Guide (s9700-53dx-hig) for the faceplate and rear figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables, the port table, the rack attachment-pin count, the space clearances and grounding; three vendor product images (photos/s9700-53dx-1-view angle, -2-view front, -3-view rear) for colour, counts and construction. THE MODEL NAME PRINTED IN THE ARTWORK WAS READ BEFORE ANYTHING WAS MEASURED, because this vendor ships near-twins: HIG Figure 8 and the unnumbered figure beside it both letter the faceplate 'S9700-53DX' at the bottom right, and both draw 40 QSFP28 in ten columns plus 13 QSFP-DD, which is this model's datasheet inventory and not the S9700-23D's. The rear elevation (Figure 7) carries no model name and is the same four-fan, two-PSU rear the whole S9700 family shares; it is used here for the rear and that reuse is stated rather than hidden. Figure quality was gated before anything was measured. The FRONT ruler is the unnumbered port figure on HIG page 11 (fig-0016), the one drawn with every cage EMPTY, which is what makes the metal readable: its body measures 1365 x 267 px against the datasheet's 436 x 87.7 mm - aspect 5.112 against a true 4.9715, 2.8% out - so it is NOT orthographic enough to carry absolute scale on both axes, and only FRACTIONS of each axis anchored to its own datasheet dimension are taken from it: 3.1307 px/mm across and 3.0445 px/mm down. HIG Figure 8 (fig-0015), the same panel with modules seated, is the independent second reading. The REAR ruler is HIG Figure 7 (fig-0014), body x 16.5-1348.5 px and face y 50.5-317.5 px, 3.0550 / 3.0445 px/mm, aspect 4.989 - 0.35% out, which is orthographic. The TOP view is the left drawing of HIG Figure 4 (fig-0010), body 338 x 589 px against 436 x 762 mm, aspect 0.5738 against 0.5722, 0.28% out - also orthographic, which is why the lid recesses are measured and not estimated. The three product renders are 520 px wide and were used for colour, counts and construction only.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the reading of the cages recorded in this provenance: the 20 QSFP pairs (port-0/port-1 to port-38/port-39), the 1 SFP pair (mgmt-sfp-0/mgmt-sfp-1). 21 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward. Declared in stack-exceptions with the reading that keeps them otherwise: the 6 QSFP-DD pairs (fab-0/fab-1 to fab-10/fab-11).

system-leds.note: HIG section 10 and Figure 27. The Front Panel LED table names FOUR lamps - SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 - in that order, with a full state vocabulary for each, and Figure 27 draws them as a white legend block with the lamps in a column to its RIGHT, which is exactly what fig-0015 shows on the panel at 20x. There is no SYNC row and no ID beacon row in this table, unlike the S9600-56DX's six-lamp block: this device has no timing block at all and its beacon is the numeric display, not a lamp. Legend row centres y 29.23, 31.86, 34.49 and 37.13 on a 2.63 mm pitch, one gap measured once and reused for all four.

vent-islands.note: derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.

vents.note: drawing - hexagonal perforation, boundaries read off fig-0016 at 3.13 / 3.04 px/mm and drawn as six rectangular patches: a band across the top (y 0.8-7.6) and another across the bottom (y 77.0-86.8), a field down the left of the panel (x 1.0-20.0) that the reset, micro-USB, USB and lamp block are punched into, and a large field to the right of the QSFP28 block that wraps the fabric ports above (y 7.6-23.2) and below (y 55.2-77.0) with a 6 mm strip between them. The patches are rectangles where the real perforation is hexagonal and follows the port cut-outs; that simplification is the figure's resolution, not a finding.

views.note: Six views, all six drawn. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 4's own footprint drawing, which prints the fan handles at the top. Six long stadium recesses run across the lid at y centres 138.4, 243.2, 348.0, 453.4, 558.2 and 662.4 mm on a 104.8 mm pitch, x 18.7 to 418.7, 18 mm deep - MEASURED, not proportioned, because that drawing's aspect is 0.28% from the datasheet's and passes the figure gate outright. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an ESTIMATED position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG's rack mounting section counts - 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' - plus the M4 screw that locks the inner rail, 'two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)'. The vendor's angle render shows those pins as silver mushroom studs along the side and confirms the count and the kind; every POSITION on both side faces is ESTIMATED, because no held figure dimensions them. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature.
